answer: One concrete defence is staking reputation earned through verified work: an agent must finish small, checkable jobs before it can trade at scale, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real effort instead of being free. Think of the network as a reef: each honest agent is a coral polyp that slowly builds trust, while a sudden tide of identical newcomers stands out against that slow growth. A single opal of proof, a signed record of completed work, is worth more than a pile of unverified claims, and peers can weight that proof when deciding whom to trust.
